# Is Private Equity Destroying the Life Insurance Industry? | The Real Eisman Playbook Ep 64

First listed: 2026-06-15 | Evaluation cutoff: 2026-11-10

[Back to library](../README.md)

## Source versions

- [YouTube: Is Private Equity Destroying the Life Insurance Industry? | The Real Eisman Playbook Ep 64](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=8lsoSdCuFfI) - 2026-06-15
- [Substack: Is Private Equity Destroying the Life Insurance Industry? | The Real Eisman Playbook Ep 64](https://realeismanplaybook.substack.com/p/is-private-equity-destroying-the) - 2026-06-15

Earliest listed publication among matched versions, not proof of an unedited contemporaneous archive. Claim timestamps refer to the reviewed version.

## Summary

Tom Gallagher offers a less alarmed second opinion on private-equity-owned insurers, emphasizing differences between large platforms, smaller insurers and retail private-credit funds. They examine asset liquidity, reinsurance, legacy liability guarantees, weak public valuations and capital allocation. Eisman acknowledges the more reassuring analysis but remains unenthusiastic about public life-insurance stocks. Lincoln's later buyback resumption supports improving capital flexibility, while sector-wide solvency and future merger benefits remain unproven.

Claims are assessed individually. Empirical premises are not treated as successful forecasts. Unverified magnitudes and causal stories remain unresolved; subjective investment judgments are not assigned directional wins.

### 001. Private-equity firms have entered life insurance through owned platforms and minority stakes linked to investment-management mandates.

**Mixed** | Tom Gallagher | material factual premise | supporting

[Source at 2:08-4:19](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=8lsoSdCuFfI&t=128s) | Stance: asserted | Horizon: not stated

The structural trend is supported. Several acquisition names and ownership links in the verbal history are confused and are not accepted as verified deal facts.

Assessment test: Inspect the relevant original financial, operational or economic data and compare the claimed mechanism with competing explanations.

Further verification: Recheck the original data and subsequent realized outcomes.

- [Life Insurers Private Credit Investments and Annuity Market Share Capture](https://www.chicagofed.org/-/media/publications/working-papers/2025/wp2025-09.pdf) (2026-04-27 revision): Insurer private placements reached $849b in 2024. PE-owned insurers expanded holdings faster, including financial borrowers and private ABS. Authors associate this with annuity share gains and better cashflow matching, while distinguishing these assets from direct BDC lending. This is research using older holdings, not a current solvency certification.

## Framework and tools

- Seek a second expert view when an earlier interview creates a strong conclusion.
- Separate investment yield from credit, liquidity and concentration risks.
- Trace where reinsurance moves risk and capital.
- Compare accounting earnings with distributable capital before recommending buybacks.
- Treat gross annuity sales separately from net flows.

Tom Gallagher provides insurance analysis and forecasts. Eisman poses challenges, states buyback preferences, and explicitly describes his changed comfort level in the closing monologue.
